source: Stats SA P0341 — Governance, Public Safety and Justice Survey (GPSJS, successor to the Victims of Crime Survey/VOCS). Operative rates: GPSJS 2024/25 release (published Aug 2025). Cross-checked against the GPSJS 2023/24 release (published Aug 2024) — the 2023/24 values match to the digit across both publications.
grainNote: GPSJS publishes reporting-to-police rates at NATIONAL grain only; provincial tables cover experience-of-crime prevalence, not reporting rates. Western Cape rates are not published, so the national rate is applied uniformly across stations — that uniformity is declared in the app (the true geography of underreporting is unknown).
method: Per station-year, unreported estimate U = R × (1 − r) / r, where R = SAPS reported count and r = the survey share of victims/households reporting SOME OR ALL incidences to the police (all + some, from the publication's own stacked-bar components).

robbery.src: GPSJS 2024/25 (P0341), Figure 51: 2024/25 reported all 35,4% + some 0,9% = 36,3% (the text's complement, 100 − 63,6% not reported, rounds to 36,4% — component sum used)
robbery.crosscheck: GPSJS 2023/24 = 44,2% in BOTH the 2023/24 release (individual reporting chart, p.18: 'Street Robbery 44,2%') and GPSJS 2024/25 Figure 51 (all 44,2% + some 0,0%).
caveats: Year-to-year swing 44,2% → 36,3% — the operative rate is the latest year, declared as such.

MAPPING: the app's robbery is SAPS aggravated + common robbery (street robbery, home robbery, business robbery, hijackings...). The survey's street-robbery rate is the closest published analogue; home robbery reports at a HIGHER rate (57,6% household-level 2023/24), so the estimate likely overstates unreported home-robbery within the aggregate.

sexoff.src: GPSJS 2024/25 (P0341), Table 37: percentage of individuals who reported all or some incidences of sexual offences to the police, 2024/25 = 56,3%
sexoff.crosscheck: GPSJS 2023/24 = 67,5% in BOTH the 2023/24 release (individual reporting chart, p.18) and GPSJS 2024/25 Table 37. Series: 56,0% (2022/23, sample flagged small) · 67,5% (2023/24) · 56,3% (2024/25).
caveats: FLOOR: victimisation surveys themselves under-capture sexual offences (disclosure to an interviewer is a barrier, and the survey covers only individuals 16+) — GPSJS 2024/25 measures just 60 000 incidences nationally while SAPS records similar volumes REPORTED. The estimate is a floor on the true unreported count, never a measure of it.
Small survey sample (Table 37 flags earlier years '*: sample too small, CVs too high'); rate swings 56 ↔ 67,5 across three years.

carjacking.surveyCategory: Hijacking of a motor vehicle, individuals, victim-level
carjacking.src: GPSJS 2024/25 (P0341), Figure 68: 2024/25 reported all 76,8% (no 'some' band published; 23,2% reported none)
carjacking.crosscheck: GPSJS 2023/24 = 65,4% in BOTH the 2023/24 release (individual reporting chart, p.18: 'Hijacking 65,4%') and GPSJS 2024/25 Figure 68.
caveats: Year-to-year swing 65,4% → 76,8% on a small victim base (GPSJS 2024/25: 102 000 hijacking victims nationally) — the operative rate is the latest year, declared as such.

excluded.murder: Near-fully recorded — GPSJS 2023/24 household reporting chart (p.9): 100,0% of households that experienced murder reported it to the police. No unreported estimate is meaningful; a body is counted whether or not anyone files a report.
excluded.commercial: Business/commercial crime falls outside the GPSJS household and individual survey scope — no survey reporting rate exists. EXCLUDED, never guessed.
